attempts.sql: SELECT c.symbol_id AS symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS method_count FROM code.symbols c JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.line_start > c.line_start AND m.line_end <= c.line_end WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND c.file_id NOT IN (SELECT file_id FROM code.files WHERE is_test) GROUP BY c.symbol_id, c.line_start, c.line_end HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, symbol_id ASC

request:
Which classes in the non-test code define at least 20 methods directly in their own body? Count every method definition separately (a property getter and its setter count as two; inherited methods and methods of nested classes do not count). Return each class's symbol ID and its method count, largest count first, ties broken by symbol ID alphabetically.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), method_count (integer). Order the rows as the question asks.
explanation: Joins each non-test class symbol to method symbols in the same file whose line range falls strictly within the class's line range, which captures directly defined methods while excluding nested classes' methods (whose line ranges are not within the outer class's own body span) and inherited methods. It groups by class, keeps those with at least 20 such methods, and orders by descending count then symbol ID. Test files are excluded via code.files.is_test.
sql: SELECT c.symbol_id AS symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS method_count FROM code.symbols c JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.line_start > c.line_start AND m.line_end <= c.line_end WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND c.file_id NOT IN (SELECT file_id FROM code.files WHERE is_test) GROUP BY c.symbol_id, c.line_start, c.line_end HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, symbol_id ASC
